content:
We have list of isomers SMILES. Need to find which matches NMR data: carbon shifts include carbonyl at 166, many aromatic carbons, ethoxy CH2 61, CH3 14. So need ethoxy group (CCO). Among candidates, look for "CCO" pattern. Let's examine each:

1. 'CC1=C(OC2=C(C1=O)C=C(C=C2)C(=O)OC)C(=O)OC' - has CC at start (ethyl attached to aromatic carbon?), but also multiple C(=O)OC (methyl esters). Contains OCH3 not CH2. No CH2 at 61.

2. 'CC1=CC=C(C=C1)COC2=COC(=CC2=O)OC(=O)O' - has CC aromatic (ethyl attached to phenyl), also OCH2? "COC2" indicates CH2-O-? Actually "COC2" is -CH2-O- attached to aromatic. That CH2 would be 61 ppm maybe. Also has a carboxylic acid OC(=O)O. Contains OCH3? Not.

3. 'CC1=C[C@@]2([C@@H](C1=O)O)C3=C(C(=CC(=C3)OC)O)C(=O)O2' - has CC at start attached to aromatic, but not ethoxy.

4. 'CCOC(=O)C1=CC2=C(C=CC(=C2)C(=O)OC)OC1=O' - This has CCOC(=O) (ethyl ester) and also another C(=O)OC (methyl ester). So extra OCH3.

5. 'CC(=O)CC1=C(C2=C(C(=CC(=C2)OC)O)C(=O)C1=O)O' - has acetyl not ethoxy.

6. 'C1C(OC2=CC=CC=C2O1)C(C3=CC=C(O3)C(=O)O)O' - no ethoxy.

7. 'COC1=C2C(=C(C(=C1)C(=O)O)OC)C=CC=C2C(=O)O' - has methoxy.

8. 'C1=CC(=C(C=C1CC2=CC(=C(C=C2O)O)C(=O)O)O)O' - has CC attached to aromatic (ethyl side chain) but not ethoxy.

9. 'COC1=CC(=CC(=C1O)O)C(=O)C2=CC(=CC(=C2)O)O' - methoxy.

10. 'C1C[C@]2(C(=CC3=C(C=C(C=C3O2)O)O)C1=O)CC(=O)O' - no ethoxy.

We need ethoxy CH2-CH3 attached to carbonyl (ester). That is pattern "CCOC(=O)" as in candidate 4 and maybe 2? Candidate 4: "CCOC(=O)C1=CC2=..." has ethyl ester. Also has another methyl ester (C(=O)OC). That would give extra OCH3 carbon at ~55, which we don't see. So maybe not.

Candidate 2: "CC1=CC=C(C=C1)COC2=COC(=CC2=O)OC(=O)O". Contains "CC1=..." ethyl attached to phenyl (alkyl substituent) not ethoxy. Also "COC2" is CH2-O- attached to aromatic, giving CH2 at 61, but the CH3 is part of the ethyl on phenyl (CH3-CH2-). That CH2 attached to aromatic would be ~30, not 61. So not.

Thus maybe the correct SMILES is not in list? Could be missing.

But we can still validate candidate 4: get formula.
